question.text:
If p: 2 is an even number
$\mathrm{q}: 2$ is a prime number,
$\mathrm{r}: 2+2=2^2$
Then the symbolic statement $p \rightarrow(q \vee r)$ means

options.text: 2 is an even number and 2 is a prime number or$2+2=2^2$
2 is an even number then 2 is a prime number or $2+2=2^2$.
2 is an even number or 2 is a prime number then $2+2=2^2$
If2 is not even number then 2 is a primenumber $\alpha=2+2=2^2$

solution.text: $\mathrm{p} \rightarrow(\mathrm{q} \vee \mathrm{r})$. If 2 is even number then 2 is a prime number or $2+2=2^2$.
